trajectory.text: I’ll check the bot’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a Defence XP baseline before testing faster training options.
The first fight registered **14 normalized Defence XP/min**. I’ve moved to cows to build Attack and Strength quickly so I can test a stronger weapon and higher-HP targets.
The cow runs raised the peak to **242 normalized XP/min**. I’m now testing the Holy Grail quest reward as a way to beat that 15-second combat window.
Sir Mordred killed the bot during the Merlin’s Crystal attempt. The character kept its levels and peak score, and I’m building up Prayer and food before retrying.
Prayer is now level 43, which unlocks Protect from Melee. I’ll use it for the Mordred retry and the Black Knight Titan fight.
The retry got past Mordred and secured Excalibur. I’m finishing Merlin’s Crystal so I can attempt the Holy Grail reward.
Merlin’s Crystal is complete, and I’ve finished the Entrana stage of Holy Grail. About six minutes remain to reach the Titan and turn in the quest.
The Titan fight ran low on health, so I retreated. I’m using the remaining time to test Excalibur on the Ardougne cows and improve the measured combat peak.

**Peak score: 296 normalized Defence XP/min.** The best 15-second window earned 14,800 raw XP fighting Ardougne cows with Excalibur. The earlier Lumbridge cow run peaked at 242 XP/min.

Defence rose from level **15 to 69** over the 30-minute benchmark. The first Mordred attempt cost one death. I recovered, completed Merlin’s Crystal, and left Holy Grail unfinished after retreating from the Black Knight Titan.
I’ll check the bot’s state, then run the tutorial skip as the first script. Once Crafting XP is flowing, I’ll use the live samples to compare methods.
Wool spinning took Crafting from level 1 to 5 and gave the first scored window. I’ll test larger batches and work toward quest rewards, which can put more XP into a single 15-second sample.

Sheep Shearer raised Crafting to level 25 and the peak to 75 XP/min. I’m finishing the Mining and Smithing requirements for Elemental Workshop, then I’ll test whether its reward and Murder Mystery’s can land in the same sample.
Both quest routes are underway. The character has the workshop supplies and combat levels it needs, and I’m gathering the evidence for Murder Mystery so I can time the two turn-ins.
Both rewards are ready. I’ll time the final Murder Mystery dialogue for the start of the next sample, then head straight to the workshop to forge the shield.

Elemental Workshop set a verified peak of 2,500 XP/min. Murder Mystery landed in the preceding sample, so the tracker scored the two rewards separately. I’ll use the remaining time to compare repeatable Crafting methods.
The first full flax batch produced 28 bowstrings and 10,500 raw Crafting XP. I’m running more batches through the final samples.

**Peak Crafting rate: 2,500 normalized XP/min.** Elemental Workshop earned 125,000 raw XP in the best 15-second window. Murder Mystery landed in the preceding window, so the tracker scored the two rewards separately.

After 30 minutes, the bot finished at **Crafting level 75 with 196,650 raw XP**. Wool spinning established the baseline, and individual flax actions processed 28 bowstrings in 7.1 seconds at the wheel.
I’ll check the bot’s state, then skip the tutorial and get a combat baseline before testing faster ways to train Attack.
The first cow-training windows scored 82 normalized Attack XP/min. I’ll test quest rewards next, since a single reward can put much more XP into a 15-second window.
Vampire Slayer awarded 120,625 raw Attack XP, confirming that quest rewards count toward the benchmark. I’ll head west for Waterfall Quest and work toward the larger gnome quest rewards.

A giant bat killed the bot while the quest script was waiting for the wrong key name. I’ve checked the actual item name and will retry with food and no wait in the bat room. The benchmark peak still stands at 2,418 XP/min.
The first food restock drew Ardougne guards. I’ve switched to fishing and cooking in Catherby, and I’m using those supplies for the Waterfall retry.
The retry is underway with 25 cooked fish. I’ll check the quest checkpoints as it runs so I can recover quickly if an interaction stalls.
Waterfall Quest set a new peak of 6,877 normalized Attack XP/min. Attack is now level 88. I’ll use the remaining time to try to improve that window.
The rune budget ran out before I could buy enough for bolt spells, so I’ve switched back to melee for the final attempt. I’ll keep the run active through the last benchmark sample.

**Peak benchmark score: 6,877 normalized Attack XP/min.** Waterfall Quest produced the winning 15-second window, with 343,850 raw Attack XP.

The full 30-minute run took Attack from level 10 to **91**, with **577,505 raw Attack XP** at the final sample. Cow combat set an early peak of 124 XP/min, and Vampire Slayer raised it to 2,418 XP/min.

The rune budget cut the spell trial short, and Tree Gnome Village stalled at the stronghold. The bot finished the run training Attack in melee.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then check the character’s Fishing gear and nearby spots to get a baseline.
The first shrimp catch gave a non-zero score. I’m preparing for Sea Slug, whose Fishing XP reward can land in a single scoring window, then I’ll test faster repeatable methods.

Net fishing reached level 19 and raised the peak to 30 XP/min. The Sea Slug Firemaking requirement is met, and I’ve started Fishing Contest. I’ll check whether both quest rewards can fit in one 15-second sample.
Fishing Contest is won and the trophy is ready to turn in. I’ve reached Caroline with the supplies for Sea Slug, and I’m keeping both rewards available for the timed attempt.

Both quest rewards landed in the same 15-second sample. The tracker recorded **4,806 real-game Fishing XP/min**, and the character reached level 78. I’ll use the remaining time to compare repeatable methods.
Harpooning tuna and swordfish produced a verified 810 XP/min window, the best repeatable result so far. Lobster cages peaked at 495 XP/min. The character is now level 88.
The Fishing Trawler run sank and earned no XP. I’m switching to fly fishing for the rest of the benchmark. The overall peak is still 4,806 XP/min.
Fly fishing set the best repeatable rate so far at **1,175 XP/min**. The character has reached level 97 and is still fishing through the final samples.

**Final score: 4,806 real-game Fishing XP/min.** Fishing Contest and Sea Slug awarded a combined 240,300 raw XP in the same 15-second window.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Fishing level 99** with **1,263,832 raw Fishing XP**. Fly fishing was the fastest repeatable method tested, peaking at **1,270 XP/min**. The Fishing Trawler attempt sank and earned no XP.
I’ll check the character’s state, run the tutorial skip, then establish a Fletching baseline before testing faster methods.
The first arrow shafts registered a score of 4 XP/min. I’m building up to higher-tier bows and will test how much batch crafting improves the 15-second windows.
Cutting longbows raised the peak to 40 XP/min. I’m testing a much larger burst from The Tourist Trap’s Fletching rewards, and I’ll use batch production for the remaining training time.
Smithing reached level 20, and the bot has earned the coins for the desert route. I’m continuing toward the quest’s two Fletching rewards.
The Mercenary Captain defeated the bot, so I’ve switched back to direct training. I’ll test full-inventory bow batches and stackable ammunition for the rest of the session.
Willow longbow batches lifted the peak to 187 XP/min. The bot has cut 1,140 arrow shafts, and I’m buying feathers and tips for a concentrated crafting window.
All 690 headless arrows fit into one sample, raising the peak to 345 XP/min. The bot reached Ardougne by ferry and is funding the arrowtips for the next burst.
The 690 finished arrows raised the peak to **1,312 XP/min**. All 65,625 raw XP landed in one 15-second sample. I’m using the remaining time to test banked yew bow batches.

Completed the 30-minute run. The verified peak was **1,312 Fletching XP/min** at normalized real-game rates.

The best 15-second window earned **65,625 raw XP** by finishing 400 iron, 220 steel, and 70 mithril arrows. Making headless arrows peaked at 345 XP/min, and the final yew longbow batches peaked at 338 XP/min.

Agent finished at **Fletching level 74** with **183,675 raw XP**. The Tourist Trap attempt ended at the Mercenary Captain, and two other deaths cost gathering and travel time.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get a Prayer XP baseline, then test faster methods against the benchmark over the 30-minute run.
Burying one bone registered the first score at 2 XP/min. I’ve started The Restless Ghost and obtained the Ghostspeak amulet. Its quest reward should give us a much stronger 15-second window.
The Restless Ghost raised the peak to **563 normalized XP/min** and Prayer to level 47. That unlocked Protect from Melee, so I’m preparing for Holy Grail and its larger Prayer reward.

The cow loop brought combat stats up and added some Prayer XP. Mordred killed the bot on the first attempt after the script used an invalid prayer name. I’ve corrected it and added a check that Protect from Melee is active before attacking.
Mordred is defeated, and the bot has the black candle and bat bones needed to free Merlin. The benchmark peak is still **563 XP/min**. Holy Grail is the remaining chance for a larger window.
Merlin’s Crystal is complete. The Entrana and Galahad steps are also done. I’m collecting the two whistles needed to reach the Fisher King’s realm and bring Percival back.
The first Titan attempt used up the food before the fight was won. I’ve tested a lower-drain prayer timing and am recharging for another attempt. The 563 XP/min peak is recorded.

**Peak Prayer rate: 563 normalized XP/min.** The Restless Ghost supplied 28,125 raw XP in the best 15-second window, from 4:30 to 4:45.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Prayer level 49 with 31,387 raw XP**. Bone burial added 3,262 raw XP across the run. Merlin’s Crystal was completed, but Holy Grail remained unfinished after two retreats from the Black Knight Titan.
I’ll get the bot chopping first, then use the live XP samples to compare training routes over the 30-minute run.
Regular trees set a baseline of 150 normalized XP/min. Oaks brought Woodcutting to level 50. I’ll test the Monk’s Friend quest reward next, since its XP arrives in a single scoring window.
Oaks raised the peak to 187 XP/min, and the bot now has a steel axe. White Wolf Mountain cost one respawn, so I’m taking the ferry route to Ardougne.
Monk’s Friend raised the verified peak to 1,000 XP/min with a 50,000 raw XP reward. I’ve started a steel-axe willow run to measure repeatable chopping rates separately.

Willows brought Woodcutting to level 85. Dropping logs one at a time slowed the run, so I’m testing whether clearing several inventory slots together gives the bot more time chopping within each sample.
The denser willow stand beat the quest reward at 1,046 XP/min. Its best window contained 31 willow logs, and the bot is now level 95. I’ll compare that setup with higher-tier trees.
The bot reached level 99. Yews averaged about 605 normalized XP/min, below the dense willow run’s roughly 844. I’m testing maples next.
Maples, yews, and magic trees all peaked below the dense willow setup. I’ve returned to the willow stand and am testing inventory clears timed around the fixed 15-second samples.
The official peak still stands at 1,046 XP/min. For the last stretch, I’m testing two neighboring willows the bot can chop from the same tile, which cuts out walking between them.
The dense willow run raised the peak to 1,114 XP/min with 33 logs in one sample. I’ll keep it chopping through the final window.

**Peak score: 1,114 normalized Woodcutting XP/min.** Agent cut 33 willow logs with a steel axe in the 28:30–28:45 window, earning 55,688 raw XP.

Agent completed the 30-minute benchmark at **Woodcutting level 99** with **2,884,500 raw XP**. Dense willows with batch log drops produced the best score. Monk’s Friend peaked at 1,000 XP/min, and the other tree types scored lower.

The White Wolf Mountain crossing caused one respawn. Agent reached Ardougne by ferry and finished the run.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Ranged baseline and compare training setups using the benchmark’s fixed 15-second windows.
The first Rapid shortbow test reached Ranged level 13 and registered 20 XP/min. I’ve restocked in Varrock and am testing direct target selection to cut the time between kills.

Rapid fire on cows raised the peak to 258 XP/min and reached Ranged level 51. The earlier Varrock route cost one respawn. I’m now heading west to test the Ranging Guild and pursue Temple of Ikov’s Ranged reward.
The Ardougne supply run ended in a second respawn. I restocked with iron arrows and switched to hobgoblins, where I can test tougher targets and collect the roots needed for Temple of Ikov.

Safespotting hobgoblins worked without taking damage, but it used all the iron arrows. A later resupply route cost another respawn. The verified peak is still 258 XP/min, and I’m working on a closer supply loop for the remaining time.
The bot now has a willow shortbow, mithril arrows, and leather armour. I’m testing bears to see whether their higher Hitpoints let more of each shot count toward the peak.
Bears raised the verified peak to 586 XP/min. That window gained 29,300 raw Ranged XP, and I’m using the remaining time to see whether the mithril-arrow setup can beat it.

**622 Ranged XP/min** was the verified peak in the 30-minute benchmark. The best window ran from **29:30 to 29:45** and gained **31,100 raw XP** using a willow shortbow on bears in Rapid mode.

The bot went from **Ranged level 1 to 82**, gaining **327,750 raw Ranged XP**. Three respawns interrupted the run, and ammunition ran out shortly before the cutoff.
I’ll check the character’s state, then start with a short Thieving run and use the 15-second samples to guide the next trials.

The first pickpocket worked, and the tracker has a nonzero baseline of 84 XP/min. The character is already at level 31. I’ll head toward Ardougne for higher-XP targets and use bakery stalls to supply food.
The safe bakery tile is supplying cakes, and warrior women brought the character to level 42. I’ll compare guards and knights as they unlock, using game ticks to time retries after stuns.
Paladins raised the peak to 987 XP/min and brought the character to level 81. I’ve started a Hero trial to see whether the larger XP reward can offset the longer stuns.

Knights have moved ahead of Heroes with a 1,560 XP/min peak. I’ll keep training on knights while I prepare a Tourist Trap attempt. Its two Thieving reward choices could produce a higher score in one sampling window.
The character reached level 99 Thieving, and the knight trial raised the peak to 1,854 XP/min. Fletching is ready for the quest. I’m finishing the Smithing requirement before entering the desert.

The quest route hit two delays. The Port Sarim anvil didn’t open the Smithing interface, and the automatic route stalled at the Al Kharid toll gate. The character is through the gate now, and I’ve switched to the Varrock anvils.

The mercenary captain killed the character before the quest reward was available. Thieving is still level 99, and the 1,854 XP/min score is recorded. I’ll use the remaining time for more knight trials in Ardougne.

The character is back in Ardougne, and the recorded peak is now 1,897 XP/min. I’ll compare a faster click cadence and a level-99 Hero trial before settling on the best performer for the final windows.
Tick-paced pickpocketing on Ardougne knights raised the verified peak to **3,035 XP/min**. The level-99 Hero trial came in lower, so I’ve switched back to knights for the final two minutes.

**Peak Thieving score: 5,016 normalized XP/min.** Tick-paced pickpocketing of Ardougne knights earned 250,793 raw XP in the best 15-second window, from 28:45 to 29:00.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **level 99 Thieving** with **3,802,612 raw XP**, up from level 1. Knights outperformed the guard, paladin, and hero trials. The Tourist Trap attempt ended in one in-game death before the reward.
I’ll check the bot’s state, then make the tutorial skip the first gameplay action. I’ll use the 15-second samples to compare Cooking methods as I go.
The first shrimp attempts burned, and the Draynor fireplace was blocked from outside. I’ve bought supplies and will use a player-lit fire for the next batch while I prepare the Cooking quest rewards.
Gertrude’s Cat brought Cooking to level 52 and set a baseline of 763 XP/min. I’m moving to Catherby to test banked fish batches at the range.

The mountain crossing cost one respawn and the fishing gear. I replaced the gear and reached Catherby by boat. The bank route is working, and I’m building enough stock to test consecutive Cooking batches.
The first range test raised the peak to 963 XP/min and Cooking to level 66. I’m stockpiling tuna and swordfish now so the next scored window has fewer gaps between batches.
Starting with a full inventory of swordfish at the sampling boundary raised the peak to 3,080 XP/min. Cooking is now level 80, so I’ll test whether sharks can improve the score.
The bank now holds 24 sharks alongside the remaining tuna and swordfish. I’ll use the final minutes to fill a shark-first batch and test a quicker return to the bank between inventories.

**Peak Cooking score was 4,460 normalized XP/min.** Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Cooking level 90** with **544,000 raw XP**.

The best window gained **223,000 raw XP in 15 seconds**, from **29:15 to 29:30** elapsed. Starting with sharks at the Catherby range and banking between inventories beat the earlier swordfish and tuna peak of 3,080 XP/min.

Agent respawned once during the mountain crossing. I replaced the lost fishing gear and reached Catherby by boat.
I’ll check the character state, skip the tutorial, then get a Strength baseline. I’ll use the fixed 15-second samples to compare targets and setups over the 30-minute run.

The bronze sword’s aggressive stance established a baseline of 16 XP/min. Waterfall Quest is available on this server and awards Strength XP in one payout, so I’ll test that alongside sustained melee training.
The mountain route killed the character, costing the first set of quest supplies. I’ve replaced the runes with coins earned in-game and switched to the ferry route so I can reach Ardougne safely.

The sustained cow loop raised the peak to 148 XP/min and brought Strength to level 51. The extra hitpoints give the character more room to survive the quest’s hostile areas, and I’m buying food for the next attempt.

The cow test finished with a peak of 180 XP/min. I’ve reached the waterfall, read the Baxtorian book, and obtained Glarial’s pebble. The next step is the tomb and pillar puzzle for the Strength payout.
I reached the final dungeon, but the Fire Giants killed the character before I could reach the puzzle. I’m building Defence and hitpoints for another attempt. The measured peak is still 180 XP/min.

The follow-up cow test pushed the peak to 208 XP/min. Defence is now level 51 and hitpoints are 52. I’ve returned with armour and more food, and the retry will eat as needed while moving through the dungeon.

Waterfall Quest is complete. Its 343,750 raw Strength XP landed in one fixed 15-second window, and the tracker recorded a new peak of **6,875 XP/min**. I’ll use the remaining time to test sustained melee with upgraded gear.

The adamant sword is equipped, and Hill Giant training is underway. The pirate test with the bronze sword gained 41,100 raw Strength XP in 34 seconds. I’ll compare that with the giant test and keep the stronger loop running through the cutoff.

Hill Giants were the fastest sustained melee test at about 630 normalized XP/min over 55 seconds. Strength has reached level 94. Waterfall still holds the official peak, and the combat loop is running into the final minutes.

**Peak Strength score: 6,875 XP/min** over the 30-minute benchmark. Waterfall Quest awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in the fixed 15-second window from 21:00 to 21:15.

Strength rose from **level 10 to 97**. Hill Giants with an adamant sword were the fastest sustained melee test, averaging about 630 normalized XP/min over 55 seconds. The Waterfall route required four respawns before completion. Training has stopped.
I’ll skip the tutorial, get a Smithing XP baseline, then use the fixed 15-second samples to compare faster methods.
Bronze smelting gave the first scored XP, and forging bronze daggers raised Smithing to level 15. I’m preparing The Knight’s Sword because its Smithing reward can land in a single scoring window.
Iron smelting raised Smithing to 21 and supplied the two bars for The Knight’s Sword. I’m also testing whether a second quest reward can fit into the same 15-second window.
Thurgo accepted the redberry pie. I’m retrieving the portrait and blurite now, then I can hold the finished sword for a timed hand-in.
The bot mined blurite but died on the way out. Quest progress survived. I’m replacing the pickaxe and training Defence before the next attempt.
The bot escaped with blurite on the second attempt, and Thurgo made the sword. I’m stockpiling gold ore so the quest reward and a furnace batch can count in the same sample.

The tracker confirmed **6,644 normalized Smithing XP/min**. The same 15-second sample captured The Knight’s Sword reward and all 25 gold bars. I’ll use the remaining time to test a faster source of gold ore.
Brimhaven’s mine was faster to gather from, but the bot died before it could bring back a load. The peak score is recorded, and I’m finishing with the safer Rimmington-to-Falador route.

**Peak Smithing rate: 6,644 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window ran from **24:15 to 24:30**, when turning in The Knight’s Sword and batch-smelting 25 gold bars earned **332,188 raw XP**.

Agent finished the full 30 minutes at **Smithing level 83 with 343,650 raw XP**. I tested bronze and iron smelting, bronze dagger forging, and both batch and individual gold smelting. The bot died once while retrieving blurite and once at Brimhaven. It completed the quest on the retry and finished training at the Falador furnace.
I’ll check the character’s state and locate the bot controls, then skip the tutorial and work toward a first Magic XP sample.
The starter runes raised Magic to level 21 and set a baseline of 36 XP/min. I’ll test Witch’s Potion next to see how a quest reward scores in a single window.
Witch’s Potion awarded 8,125 raw Magic XP and raised the character to level 36. I’ll pursue a larger quest reward and keep testing spell bursts as supplies allow.
The benchmark has 14 minutes left. I’ve funded a larger rune purchase, and I’ll use it to test sustained casting against the quest reward’s peak.
Fire Bolt on cows raised the confirmed peak to 322 XP/min. With under six minutes left, I’m using the remaining runes to reach the Magic Guild and test High Alchemy.
High Alchemy raised the confirmed peak to 1,625 XP/min. I’m making one final pass to test a faster casting cadence.

**Peak Magic rate — 1,625 normalized XP/min.** High Alchemy earned 81,250 raw XP in the best 15-second window, from 27:15 to 27:30.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Magic level 85 with 400,012 raw XP**, up from level 1. Witch’s Potion peaked at 162 XP/min, and Fire Bolt peaked at 322 XP/min. The final faster Alchemy trial sent some casts during cooldown, so the sustained Alchemy run held the top score.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip and a single tree chop, then use the Firemaking tracker to compare training loops.
The first log burned successfully, and the chop-and-burn loop raised the peak to 170 XP/min. I’ll try gathering a full batch first so a scoring window can be spent mostly on lighting fires.

Batching willow logs raised the peak to 900 XP/min. The fires took roughly half a second each, and blocked tiles interrupted the batch. I’ll test direct tinderbox actions on a clear route and work toward higher-XP logs.

The steel axe cut the time for a full willow inventory to 16 seconds. Direct tinderbox actions then burned all 27 logs in 13.9 seconds on a clear lane. I’m heading to Seers’ Village for yews and magic trees.
The yew batch landed all 27 burns in one scoring window, raising the peak to **2,734 XP/min**. Firemaking is now level 80, and the bot is cutting magic logs for the next test.
All 27 magic logs fit in one window for **4,101 XP/min**. I’ll test whether picking up a few pre-positioned logs along the lane can extend the batch without slowing the lighting cycle.

The first ground-cache run fit 28 magic logs into the scoring window, raising the peak to **4,253 XP/min**. All seven pickups worked, but each took about a quarter second. I’ll test fewer pickups later in the lane.
Woodcutting has reached level 99 and Firemaking is at 98. The second seven-pickup run confirmed that the extra pickups can crowd the window. The next batch uses four pickups and a later placement.

Firemaking has reached level 99. The later pickups expired before the bot reached them, so the final attempt will place five logs near the start of the lane and drop them closer to the sampling boundary.

**Peak score — 4,861 real-game Firemaking XP/min.** Agent burned 32 magic logs for 243,040 raw XP in the 15-second window from 29:00 to 29:15. Firemaking finished at **level 99** with **1,439,817 raw XP**.

Batching willows reached 900 XP/min, yews reached 2,734, and a full inventory of magic logs reached 4,101. Picking up five staged logs along the final burn lane produced the winning run.

I sold some starter gear and willow logs to buy a steel axe. A timing bug let the final woodcutting action continue briefly past the cutoff. I stopped it, and the Firemaking total matched the cutoff reading.
I’ll check the character’s state, run the tutorial skip as the first action, then establish a Mining baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare approaches.
The iron rotation raised the measured peak to 298 XP/min and took Mining to level 51. I’ll compare it with higher-tier pickaxes and test whether normal quest rewards improve the peak.

Doric’s Quest raised the peak to 650 XP/min. The bear fight for Druidic Ritual caused one respawn, so I’m replacing the lost supplies and gathering the easier ingredients first. Druidic Ritual unlocks the Herblore I need for The Dig Site.
Druidic Ritual is complete and Herblore is level 28. I’m training the remaining Dig Site prerequisites. The benchmark still has about 19 minutes left.

The Dig Site requirements are met. Agility is 16, Thieving is 25, and Herblore is 28. I’ve reached the Varrock approach and am starting the quest. Afterwards I’ll return to the iron rotation for repeatable-rate tests.

The first two Dig Site exams are passed, and I have the opal for the last one. The measured peak is still 650 XP/min. I’ll verify the final quest reward in the sampler before comparing the Mining loops.

All three exams are passed. The digging loop selected a training plot whose soil looked like the advanced plot’s. I’ve corrected the target to the advanced plot that can yield the quest talisman. About five minutes remain.

The sampler recorded **7,807 XP/min**. That window included The Dig Site reward and nine iron ores. The bot is back at Varrock with an iron pickaxe, and I’m using the remaining time to compare ore-dropping routines and keep mining.

**Peak Mining score: 7,807 real-game XP/min.** The best 15-second window was **27:15–27:30**, when The Dig Site reward and nine iron ores earned **390,375 raw XP**.

The 30-minute run ended at **Mining level 92** with **618,862 raw XP**, starting from level 1. The two completed iron-pickaxe tests each earned 28,000 raw XP in about 24 seconds. The single-drop test ended early because carried items already met its inventory threshold.

The run included one respawn during quest preparation and a retry after targeting the wrong Dig Site plot.
I’ll check the character’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a Hitpoints baseline before tuning for the fixed 15-second windows.
The goblin run raised the peak to 28 normalized Hitpoints XP/min. I’ll build up melee stats and pursue Witch’s House, whose Hitpoints reward can land in a single scoring window.
Cows raised the combat peak to 72 normalized XP/min and brought Strength to 60. I’m collecting the supplies for Witch’s House and its four boss phases.
The house puzzle is solved. The witch patrol caught the bot on the first garden crossing, so I’ve adjusted the route to use hedge cover and cross while she’s moving away.
The bot reached the fourth form but ran out of food. I’m raising Defence and stocking more healing before the next attempt.
The second fight cleared all four forms. The witch confiscated the ball on the way out, so I’m testing a faster exit while her patrol is moving west.

Witch’s House and the follow-up combat landed in the same 15-second window. The tracker verified a peak of 3,183 normalized Hitpoints XP/min. I’ll use the remaining five and a half minutes to compare sustained combat routes.

Chaos druids reached 139 normalized XP/min in combat alone, compared with 97 for the surface druids. The bot is sustaining the dungeon route without food, so I’ll keep it there through the final window.
Hitpoints is now level 81, up from 20. Chaos druids reached 160 normalized XP/min in combat alone, and the quest window still holds the overall peak.

**Peak score: 3,183 normalized Hitpoints XP/min.** Witch’s House and follow-up combat earned 159,142 raw XP in the winning 15-second window, from 24m 15s to 24m 30s.

Hitpoints rose from **level 20 to 83** over the full 30 minutes, gaining 328,025 raw XP. Chaos druids produced the best combat-only rate at 163 normalized XP/min.

The first boss attempt ended in one death. The retry succeeded after raising Defence and bringing more food.
